producer_report.summary: Planning no longer fills fields by default. Root cause: plan-entry construction copied an unread request's first line into acceptance and defaulted the rung to Implementation, so the refusal gate almost never fired. Acceptance now comes only from explicit bullets or a reading's criteria (a declined reading has none). The rung is the proposal's rung, else inferred from evidence in the request or reading, else flagged missing. Open questions are filled by lookup: a touched path absent at the base commit (a file a reading creates is excepted), and a referenced job id not in the records. A flagged item names its missing fields and a reason, and is not in Plan::order. Drain's planning pass now reads each unread request whose own words leave the plan incomplete, within the budget and job limit, then plans it again from the reading. A specifiable request then runs with no second reading, and a vague one is refused with a reason and never run. That removes the deadlock where unread items were refused and stayed queued. A new `athena plan [--budget USD] [--json]` command runs the same pass and prints the plan without working anything (default read budget $2, 0 reads nothing). The pass is deterministic Rust and calls no model. plan::trace and GapLog are still not wired to records, which the docs say. I touched display.rs (refusal reason, plan output) and main.rs (plan command, drain help) beyond plan.rs, reading.rs and drain.rs. D105 in docs/decisions.md is revised, and README, architecture and CHANGELOG are updated. I did not verify the pass against a real model: tests use the fake agent and stubs.

open_issues: `cargo run -- plan` as written in the criterion errors on the two-binary workspace; `cargo run --bin athena -- plan` is the working form. I did not edit the manifest, since that is outside the deliverables.

A refused item that was read leaves the queue and the refusal is only in the drain report. It is not written to a record, so `athena plan` after a drain no longer lists it as an open request. It stays visible as a read or declined job.
If the real reader invents plausible criteria for a vague request, the gate cannot catch it, because it checks only that fields are present. The decision entry records this.
Rung inference is a keyword and path heuristic, so an unusual wording is flagged and needs a bullet or a correction.
plan::trace and GapLog are still not wired to records (follow-up, as the docs say).
mistakes: I tried `cat` and `tail` in Bash early on; the policy denied both and nothing ran.

My first RealSteps test asserted two Reader invocations, but the declining wrapper answers outside the scenario's counter. I fixed the assertion to count only the specified request and check the vague one through its record's reading count.
learnings: The workspace has two binaries (athena, xtask), so `cargo run -- plan` fails; use `cargo run --bin athena -- plan`. In this environment the run happens in a nested scratch copy with fake agents.
Existing drain stub tests carried plan entries with no acceptance for unread items. Under the new pass those items are read first, so the log of the 'refused' test changed.
steward::queued_work lists only jobs in state Queued. A request read by the pass leaves the queue (becomes proposed or declined), so a refused item is no longer queued afterwards.
Role::Reader invocations are counted through Scenario.invocations only for requests the scenario script handles. A custom wrapper that answers some requests itself bypasses that count.
desires: Allow reading cargo test output files in the tool-results directory; the full output was too large to view, so I reran quietly.
